name: ddc_rotator
description: NCO + complex mixer + gain vs rotator_cc + multiply_const_cc

params.initial_phase_note: (-phase_inc) mod 65536: the block advances the phase before use, so the first sample uses phase 0 like rotator_cc

float_vs_gnuradio.rationale: rotator_cc advances its phase by multiplying with a complex64 increment whose angle is off by about 2e-8 rad, so its phase drifts linearly (measured: mean error 0.07 LSB in the first 512 samples, 0.95 LSB in the last 512, max 1.4 LSB at sample 4082). The float instance computes cos/sin from the exact phase word, so this is GNU Radio's error; the bound holds for 4096 samples at |x| * gain <= 0.53.

fixed_vs_float.rationale: Phase truncated to 10 table bits: phase error power (2*pi/2^10)^2/3 -> 49.0 dB. Per sample |x| * gain * 2*pi/2^10 = 106.2 LSB (|x| <= 0.66, gain 0.8) plus up to 3 LSB from the two requantizations.
Phase rounded to 10 table bits: phase error power (2*pi/2^10)^2/12 -> 55.0 dB. Per sample |x| * gain * pi/2^10 = 53.1 LSB (|x| <= 0.66, gain 0.8) plus up to 3 LSB from the two requantizations.
Phase truncated to 12 table bits: phase error power (2*pi/2^12)^2/3 -> 61.1 dB. Per sample |x| * gain * 2*pi/2^12 = 26.5 LSB (|x| <= 0.66, gain 0.8) plus up to 3 LSB from the two requantizations.
Phase rounded to 12 table bits: phase error power (2*pi/2^12)^2/12 -> 67.1 dB. Per sample |x| * gain * pi/2^12 = 13.3 LSB (|x| <= 0.66, gain 0.8) plus up to 3 LSB from the two requantizations.
